newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel may float Bank Leumi overseas.
newsitem.headline: Israel may float Bank Leumi overseas.

text.p: The Israeli government is weighing floating shares in Bank Leumi, Israel's second largest bank, in the United States and Europe, a source close to the bank privatisation process said on Monday.
"We're currently checking the possibility of floating about 10 percent," he said.

He said the offering would be based on the bank's full-year 1996 results and therefore would not occur before May 1997. He said other details, including whether the government would issue global depository receipts in London or American depository receipts in the United States, were still undecided.
Officials of MI Holdings, the government company charged with selling the government-owned shares in Israeli banks, met investment bankers in London last week to discuss an offering.
"The meetings were just for getting indications," the source said, adding the reception so far has been positive.
Some 13 percent of Leumi trades on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, where the bank as a whole has a market capitalisation of about $1.88 billion. Shareholders' equity is approximately $2.2 billion.

The government floated Leumi shares in Tel Aviv in 1993, but the slump in the domestic capital market since then has precluded further offerings. A 1994 tender to sell a controlling stake in the bank attracted only one bidder, who eventually withdrew.

In the first nine months of 1996, Leumi had a net profit of 391 million shekels. Net annualised return on equity after inflation was 7.7 percent after deducting for one-time severance payments taken for an early retirement programme.
